subject: EmberCloud private GPU pool: capacity proposal & provisioning runbook
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@embercloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing ask: private GPU pool for EmberCloud pilot

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. EmberCloud is ready to move forward with a small private deployment (VPC) to run our classification & reranking pipelines for the Q1 pilot. Before we lock procurement timelines we need help from Redwood on two things:

1) A baseline throughput & concurrency sizing recommendation that meets our latency SLOs (95th <= 150ms for short-chat prompts, 95th <= 350ms for long-run reranking flows). Expected steady-state QPS is ~350 requests/minute with occasional spikes to ~1,200 requests/minute for short windows (5-10 minutes).
2) Network egress and NAT/LB guidance — we have a constrained outbound egress budget on the VPC and need to understand whether your recommended topology introduces significant egress or connection load (we're using an internal NLB + NAT gateway).

I've attached a short requirements document that lists our expected prompt lengths and a rough call mix. Can you review and propose a provisioning plan (sizing + phased rollout + any gating checks) and share an initial runbook we can show procurement?

Attachment: ember_requirement_summary_20261118.pdf

Elena
Elena Torres

EmberCloud

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. Quick read-through looks good. To make our sizing deterministic I sketched a first-pass model and attached it (CSV) — it'll ask for expected token distribution and the two SLOs you cited. A few clarifying Qs before we finalize:

- Are the spikes you quoted (1,200 rpm) bursty from scheduled jobs or organic traffic? If scheduled, can they be shifted to a runbook window?
- Do you need multi-AZ redundancy on day 1, or is single-AZ with failover acceptable for the pilot?
- Can you confirm max prompt length (tokens) for the reranking flows? The tail has disproportionate GPU time.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow where we walk the model and I show two rollout options (thin pool vs. warm-shard approach). If that works I'll follow up afterward with a short provisioning runbook and a conservative capacity commit we can bake into procurement.

Looping in a couple operational notes from our infra side — cutting to the recommendations after the brief context:

Context / quick read: the requirements doc shows 70:30 short-chat:long-rerank mix; short-chat avg tokens ~40, rerank avg tokens ~300 with some tails to 2k. Spikes look organic (user-driven) unless you have nightly batch jobs.

Recommendations (pilot-focused):
- Baseline cluster for pilot: 4 x A40-equivalent GPUs (quantized runtime) with a staging warm pool of 1 additional GPU for fast burst absorb. That maps to expected steady QPS ~350 and gives headroom to ~800 for short spikes depending on batching efficiency.
- Burst strategy: enable a small warm-shard (single-VM per shard) we can spin up in ~90s; keep continuous prefix/KV caching for the short-chat model to preserve latency.
- Latency trade: for reranking tails, recommend a dedicated smaller batch path (lower batch size, pre-warmed KV) to avoid tail amplification.
- Networking: with NLB + NAT gateway you won't incur significant egress charges for model serving itself; however, if logs/metrics egress to external S3 buckets at high frequency that could show up. Recommend aggregating telemetry and pushing in 5s windows rather than per-request.

Phasing (minimal pilot):
1) Provision baseline 4 GPUs + warm pool 1 (single-AZ) — validation traffic only.
2) Run default workload for 72 hours with focused latency/throughput captures.
3) If 72h is clean, increase warm pool to 2 and enable autoscale policy with 2-minute cool-down; connect to production NLB routes behind feature flag.

I'll add configuration snippets to the runbook Jonas is drafting; Ben and Lauren (cc'd) will help with the procurement language for commit sizing.

marissa

Elena — following our internal sizing review and Marissa's notes above, here's a compact plan we can hand to procurement and ops. I've attached a short provisioning runbook and the run-through estimations for networking.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Pilot baseline: 4 x A40-equivalent GPUs (quantized runtime), warm pool 1; single-AZ initially. Estimated steady token cost and latency meet your 95th SLOs based on our simulated traffic (details in CSV).
- Burst capacity: warm-shard spin-up ~90s; autoscale policy to allow +2 GPUs for up to 10 minutes for organic spikes above 800 QPS.
- Networking: no additional cross-AZ egress expected for model inference. Telemetry should be batched (5s window) to avoid NAT session churn. If you plan to ship metrics to an external S3 endpoint, add 20–40 MB/min to your egress estimate for the pilot.

Attachments: provisioning_runbook_v1.md, network-egress-estimates.csv

Next steps for procurement:
1) Procurement: target a 6-month pilot commit for 4 GPUs with an opt-out after 30 days if SLA checks fail. Marissa and Ben will draft the clause.
2) Ops: we will provide an ops checklist (runbook) and a short playtest (72h).
3) DocuSign: I'll share a short PO template that you can route to your procurement team; link below.

DocuSign/PO template: https://na1.docusign.net/embercloud-po-DEAL-8342
Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-embercloud-reqs

Thanks — talk soon.
